items.author: Ole Amlor Wengler
Victor
items.body:
I had a "Did we get struck by lightning?" moment at work today. I was looking at the dump for a crash that had only happened once and traced it down to a slerp between two normalized vectors returning a 0 vector. 

That's mathematically impossible, but in the undefined case where these organic vectors are EXACTLY opposed, our code returns 0.

I double checked and they matched down the ~6th point past the decimal.

#GameDev
#Programming
#Math

items.author: Fae
items.body:
I find it interesting that people are constantly talking about more efficient ways to make software or whatever. I actively chose to do this because I get bored when things are TOO efficient lol. I wanted a playground where things are harder, but in a reasonable way. I WANT the challenge of using a language for something it wasn't ever built for. I'm constantly looking for ways to do that.

It's crazy to me that more people don't attempt stuff like this, especially beyond the most minimal of examples (like the people who made the raylib bindings for COBOL and CLIPS - they will never be used for anything and were, at best, academic exercises).

It's crazier to me that most fantasy consoles use established, popular languages. They could literally use anything, but most use Lua and JavaScript. A few use assembly. Not even a lot of love for Forth or esolangs. This is the perfect domain for this kind of fuckery.

#programming #gamedev #fantasyconsoles
